::: {#sol-three-or-eight}

An 8 closes its loops on the left, and a 3 leaves the left open.
One feature is the average ink on the left of the middle rows:
rows 2 to 5 and columns 0 to 2.
Search its cutoffs as @sol-zero-one-cutoff did, to see how well it works.

```{python}
#| code-fold: false
left_ink = images[:, 2:6, 0:3].mean(axis=(1, 2))

is_38 = (labels == 3) | (labels == 8)
cut_38, wrong_38 = best_cutoff(left_ink[is_38], labels[is_38] == 8)
print(cut_38, wrong_38, is_38.sum())
```

With a cutoff of `r py$cut_38`,
the rule gets `r py$wrong_38` of the `r sum(py$is_38)` images of 3s and 8s wrong,
`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * py$wrong_38 / sum(py$is_38))`%,
against `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * py$wrong_01 / sum(py$is_01))`% for the 0s and 1s.
The left ink of the 3s and 8s overlaps more than the center ink of the 0s and 1s,
so this pair needs a better feature, or more than one.

:::
